newsitem.title: FRANCE: Suspected ETA leader seized in France.
newsitem.headline: Suspected ETA leader seized in France.

text.p: French police captured the suspected number three leader of the Basque separatist guerrilla organisation ETA after a car chase in southwestern France, police said on Friday.
They said Jose Luis Urrusolo Sistiaga was stopped at a routine road check on Thursday night. Armed with a handgun and carrying false papers, he drove off but was caught by police.
Urrusolo Sistiaga, one of the men most wanted by Spanish police over the past decade, is suspected of being in charge of training commandos for ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom).
ETA has killed 800 people since 1968 in its bid for an independent Basque state, using bombs and shootings alongside kidnappings and extortion to finance itself.
Cooperation between France and Spain has led to more than 200 arrests in the past decade and hampered the rebels' ability to set up safe houses and arms factories in France.
The two countries have recently increased the number of meetings of their anti-terrorist experts to exchange intelligence on the guerrillas.
Earlier this week, France handed over a former ETA leader, Josu Arkauz Arana, to Spanish police after he completed a prison sentence in France. He had been in jail in France since 1991.
